title: Fusion: An Analytics Object Store Optimized for Query Pushdown
problem: Disaggregated cloud storage uses erasure coding that partitions analytics file objects into fixed-size blocks across storage nodes; when query predicates are pushed down to storage (computation pushdown), the storage system must reassemble objects across nodes, incurring high network latency that undermines pushdown's intended benefits for ad-hoc and highly-selective OLAP queries.
method: Fusion is an analytics object store that co-designs storage layout and query pushdown execution for erasure-coded environments. It reorganizes how analytics file objects (e.g., Parquet files) are partitioned and distributed across storage nodes so that query-relevant data stripes can be accessed and evaluated locally at storage nodes without full object reassembly. Pushdown execution is coordinated across storage nodes in a way that respects erasure coding boundaries, enabling predicate evaluation close to data while minimizing cross-node communication.

title: Rank-based Multi-objective Approximate Logic Synthesis via Monte Carlo Tree Search
problem: Approximate logic synthesis focuses on single objectives (delay or area), leading to local optima in multi-objective optimization under error constraints.
method: Framework uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with non-dominated circuit ranking to guide exploration of local approximate changes (LACs). A Rank-Transformer model predicts path-domain ranks, enhancing high-quality LAC application.

title: Tela: A Temporal Load-Aware Cloud Virtual Disk Placement Scheme
problem: Cloud Virtual Disk (CVD) placement algorithms for Cloud Block Storage do not account for temporal load fluctuations, leading to imbalanced storage warehouse loads, low resource utilization, and frequent overloads under dynamic workloads.
method: Tela introduces a temporal load-aware CVD placement scheme that models and predicts time-varying I/O load patterns for each physical storage warehouse, then uses these temporal load predictions to make placement decisions that balance load both at placement time and over future intervals, avoiding placements that would create future overloads.

title: Gemina: A Coordinated and High-Performance Memory Deduplication Engine
problem: Memory deduplication (via KSM) eliminates duplicate pages but forces huge pages to split into 4KB base pages, degrading TLB hit rates and memory access performance by up to 43%; asynchronous huge page promotion cannot recover this loss because deduplication breaks the uniformity of page attributes required for promotion.
method: Gemina coordinates huge page management with memory deduplication through three components: (1) a fine-grained detector that separately classifies pages by both redundancy and access hotness to decouple deduplication decisions from page-size decisions; (2) a distributor that conservatively processes pages to avoid frequent hot/cold and size-class switches; and (3) an adapter that reorganizes memory layout to enable fast base-to-huge-page conversion. Together, these components preserve huge page availability by selectively deferring or avoiding deduplication of hot pages while still capturing most memory savings.

title: VQT-CiM: Accelerating Vector Quantization Enhanced Transformer with Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory
problem: Transformer accelerators using non-volatile memory (NVM)-based compute-in-memory (CiM) for vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) face severe challenges: dynamic VMMs in attention (key-value operations) require expensive runtime write operations, compute-write-compute (CWC) dependencies, high write overhead, and limited NVM endurance degrade efficiency.
method: VQT-CiM leverages vector quantization (VQ) of transformer keys and values to convert dynamic VMMs in attention into static VMMs with learned codebooks, eliminating runtime writes. Uses residual VQ (RVQ) + product VQ (PVQ) for enhanced representation capacity and maintains accuracy. FeFET (ferroelectric FET)-based CiM crossbars with optimized dataflow and peripheral circuits execute efficient codebook lookups and static matrix multiplications without write-back cycles.

title: DCDiff: Enhancing JPEG Compression via Diffusion-based DC Coefficients Estimation
problem: Low-cost cameras cannot support learning-based compressors; one approach drops DC coefficients at camera and reconstructs them later, but statistical reconstruction methods cause deviation-introduced errors that propagate throughout the image.
method: DCDiff uses a generative diffusion model to estimate DC coefficients end-to-end rather than relying on statistical methods. It generates masks to correct image locations violating statistical distributions, suppressing error propagation. The approach maintains full JPEG compatibility with typical low-cost processors.

title: mLR: Scalable Laminography Reconstruction based on Memoization
problem: ADMM-FFT iterative reconstruction method for laminography has high accuracy but suffers from excessive computation time and large memory consumption due to repeated FFT operations.
method: Introduce memoization to replace time-consuming FFT operations by observing that similar FFT operations repeat in ADMM-FFT iterations. Apply variable offloading to save CPU memory. Scale across GPUs within and across nodes.

title: xGFabric: Coupling Sensor Networks and HPC Facilities with Private 5G Wireless Networks for Real-Time Digital Agriculture
problem: Coupling distributed low-bandwidth, unreliable sensor networks with centralized high-performance computing facilities for real-time scientific applications; sensor data has low performance/capacity but HPC offers high throughput with high latency
method: End-to-end system (xGFabric) integrating sensor networks, Private 5G networks, and HPC facilities; 5G network slicing enables low-latency, high-throughput, reliable coupling between edge and HPC

title: Necro-reaper: Pruning away Dead Memory Traffic in Warehouse-Scale Computers
problem: A significant fraction of memory traffic in warehouse-scale computers (WSC) is unnecessary: it consists of writebacks of deallocated (dead) heap data and fetches of uninitialized data, neither of which carries useful information. Short-lived heap allocations larger than a cache line—common in WSC—exacerbate this problem.
method: Necro-reaper is a software/hardware co-design that introduces new ISA instructions to let the hardware skip unnecessary dead memory traffic without requiring hardware-level tracking of live/dead data. A profile-guided compiler analyzes allocation lifetimes and annotates call sites with the new instructions. A customized memory allocator extends these annotations to inform the hardware at deallocation time. The approach leverages WSC's existing vertical integration (shared hardware, OS, compiler, and allocator stack) to make the analysis and insertion of instructions practical.

title: Using Code Coverage to Assess Feature Gaps in MPI Correctness Tool Classification Tests
problem: MPI-BugBench (MBB), a code-generator-based MPI correctness testing framework, has incomplete coverage of MPI features (e.g., varying-count collectives) and limited code structure diversity in generated tests, reducing effectiveness of testing tools like MUST, PARCOACH, and clang-tidy.
method: Analyze code coverage triggered by MBB tests in three MPI correctness tools. Use coverage analysis to identify missing MPI features and code structures. Implement 34 new tests covering previously uncovered scenarios (varying-count collectives, loops, array-based handles).

title: FlexSP: Accelerating Large Language Model Training via Flexible Sequence Parallelism
problem: Existing sequence parallelism methods for long-context LLM training assume homogeneous (equal-length) sequences and apply a single static scattering strategy, causing severe load imbalance when real training corpora have heterogeneous, long-tail sequence length distributions.
method: FlexSP introduces flexible sequence parallelism that adapts the scattering strategy per-sequence to match each sequence's actual length. The system dynamically selects the degree of sequence parallelism and the scattering pattern (e.g., how many devices a sequence is split across) based on the length distribution of the current batch, balancing workload across devices and reducing idle time from length imbalance. Communication and attention computation are co-optimized under the flexible strategy.

title: Generalizable Lithographic Hotspot Detection Using Asynchronous Meta-Learning with Only One Shot
problem: CNN-based lithographic hotspot detectors overfit and fail to generalize to unseen circuit layouts despite being trained on existing designs, limiting applicability across diverse design styles at the same technology node.
method: A few-shot meta-learning framework using asynchronous multi-task learning with a multi-gate mixture-of-experts (MMoE) model that separately updates CNN feature extraction and classification components. Layout topology-based sampling strategy enhances few-shot adaptation, enabling rapid generalization to new designs with only one training layout clip.

title: XaaS Containers: Performance-Portable Representation With Source and IR Containers
problem: Containers provide portability but sacrifice hardware-specific optimizations in HPC environments. Current containerization approaches force early-stage compilation decisions that limit performance across diverse HPC systems.
method: Proposes XaaS (Acceleration as a Service) containers using Source and Intermediate Representation (IR) representations. Delays performance-critical decisions until deployment time. Includes LLM-assisted method for automatic discovery of specializations and methodology to build container-optimized binaries for target architectures at deployment.

title: PoP-ECC: Robust and Flexible Error Correction against Multi-Bit Upsets in DNN Accelerators
problem: Continuous process scaling increases memory error severity and frequency in DNN accelerators, particularly multi-bit upsets (MBUs). Traditional single-error correction codes are insufficient for safety-critical systems.
method: Parities of Parities ECC (PoP-ECC) is a two-tier memory protection scheme. First level computes Virtual Parities (VPs) from data; second level computes Parities of Parities (PPs) from VPs. This hierarchical structure enables dynamic error correction tailored to varying error patterns with minimal overhead.

title: Tackling ML-based Dynamic Mispredictions using Statically Computed Invariants for Attack Surface Reduction
problem: ML-based runtime predictors used for code debloating and dynamic control flow monitoring lack guarantees that distinguish mispredictions from actual security attacks, making them unsuitable for safety-critical security contexts. Without this distinction, the system either blocks legitimate executions (false positives from mispredictions) or fails to stop real attacks.
method: The paper computes static program invariants at compile/analysis time to reduce the attack surface that ML-based dynamic predictors must cover. Statically proven safe behaviors are removed from the ML decision space, so the ML model only makes predictions over a reduced, ambiguous region. When the ML predictor fires on the reduced set, the probability that it is a misprediction versus an actual attack is much lower, enabling more reliable enforcement in security settings such as control flow integrity and debloating.

title: Lichen: Leveraging Coupled Heterogeneity
problem: Heterogeneous-ISA CMPs use coarse-grained uniform program phases, missing optimization across multiple heterogeneity dimensions
method: Lichen: dynamic morphing between ISA cores and execution modes (in-order/out-of-order); CART ML algorithm predicts optimal phase
